For the $N$-th order rational solution of the massive Thirring model constructed via double-Wronskian determinants, the solution describes a nonlinear superposition of $N$ distinct algebraic solitons (arising from an embedded eigenvalue of algebraic multiplicity $N$). 

When the leading-order polynomials governing the asymptotic structure have exactly $N$ real roots, these roots correspond to the $N$ well-separated asymptotic soliton centers for large $|t|$. Each fundamental algebraic soliton contributes exactly one pole in the upper half-plane of the complex $x$-plane (with a corresponding conjugate pole in the lower half-plane, ensuring regularity on the real axis). Since the $N$ solitons separate and their pole structures do not cancel in the asymptotic regime, the total number of poles in the upper half-plane is simply the number of solitons.

Thus, the number of poles in the upper half-plane scales linearly with $N$.

\boxed{N}
